2_Introduction: With this engineering, the resulting PSCs obtained a PCE of 25.3601%, a VOC of 1.181 V, FF of 83.3154%, and JSC of 25.774 mA/cm². A perovskite precursor solution was first prepared using Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 at 1.65 mol/L. A well-optimized dual-stage spin routine (1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s) was chosen to facilitate smooth and homogeneous layer formation. During the last 15 s of the second step, the anti-solvent (150 µL of CB) was dropped in the center of the substrate. The wet perovskite films were then transferred onto a hot plate and annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite—engineered with a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture to optimize Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and suppress phase segregation while maintaining a near-ideal bandgap of ~1.53 eV—proceeds through a kinetically controlled nucleation-and-growth pathway dictated by the dual-stage spin-coating protocol: the initial low-speed step (1000 rpm, 5 s) enables uniform precursor wetting and interfacial contact with the underlying charge transport layer, while the high-speed phase (5500 rpm, 30 s) governs solvent evaporation rate and supersaturation buildup, with antisolvent (150 µL chlorobenzene) introduced precisely during the final 15 s to trigger instantaneous nucleation across the entire film area, thereby suppressing heterogeneous crystal growth and minimizing pinhole formation; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 min drives complete solvent removal, promotes Ostwald ripening, and facilitates iodide redistribution to heal undercoordinated Pb²⁺ sites and iodide vacancies at grain boundaries and surfaces—processes critically reflected in the high film coverage and spatially uniform grayscale intensity observed in optical microscopy and PL mapping, which indicate negligible voids and suppressed localized non-radiative recombination centers, while the absence of residual PbI₂ peaks at ~12.6° in XRD and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection confirm phase-pure, highly crystalline, low-strain α-phase formation with enlarged grain size and reduced intragrain defect density; collectively, these morphological, optical, and structural signatures corroborate effective suppression of trap-assisted Shockley–Read–Hall recombination and enhanced carrier diffusion length, directly enabling high open-circuit voltage, short-circuit current density, fill factor, and power conversion efficiency.
